title: Is Evolution a Search Algorithm? How Life Explores Nearly Infinite Possibilities
section: 7. 可进化性：为什么有的系统更容易变出新东西 / Evolvability
text:
7. 可进化性：为什么有的系统更容易变出新东西 / Evolvability
“可进化性”（evolvability）这个词有歧义：它可以指”能产生有利突变的能力”，也可以指”能在多长时间里持续产生适应”的能力。前者更像一个静态属性（种群的突变供给有多大），后者是一个动态属性（搜索算法能不能持续找到新东西）。在搜索算法的语言里，后者才是真正的核心：一个算法的价值不在于它第一次找到解，而在于它还能不能找到第二个、第三个解。
The word “evolvability” is ambiguous: it can mean the capacity to produce favourable mutations, or the capacity to keep producing adaptation over time. The first is closer to a static property (how much mutational supply a population carries), the second is dynamical (can the search keep finding new things). In the language of search algorithms the second is the real issue: an algorithm’s value is not that it finds a solution, but that it can still find a second and a third.
最直观的两个旋钮是”变异率”和”模块化”。先看变异率：在一张崎岖的景观上，太小的变异率会让种群在少数几个局部最优之间反复停留，太大的变异率会把已经找到的好组合打散。中间存在一个最优区间，但它的位置取决于景观的崎岖程度——也就是说，最优的搜索参数是被景观决定的，而不是被算法决定的。
The two most intuitive knobs are mutation rate and modularity. Take mutation rate first: on a rugged landscape, too small a rate lets the population stall among a few local optima, while too large a rate smashes the good combinations it has already found. An optimum lies in between, but where it sits depends on ruggedness — in other words, the best search parameter is set by the landscape, not by the algorithm.


Code
ga_run <- function(model, mu, pop_size = 200, gens = 300, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  N <- model$N
  pop <- matrix(rbinom(pop_size * N, 1, 0.5), pop_size, N)
  fit <- nk_fit(model, pop)
  best <- max(fit)
  for (g in seq_len(gens)) {
    i1 <- sample.int(pop_size, pop_size, TRUE)
    i2 <- sample.int(pop_size, pop_size, TRUE)
    parents <- ifelse(fit[i1] >= fit[i2], i1, i2)
    kids <- pop[parents, , drop = FALSE]
    flip <- matrix(runif(pop_size * N) < mu, pop_size, N)
    kids[flip] <- 1 - kids[flip]
    pop <- kids
    fit <- nk_fit(model, pop)
    best <- max(best, max(fit))
  }
  best
}

mu_seq <- c(0, 0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2)
model_ga <- make_nk(20, 8, seed = 31)
ga_tbl <- tibble(mu = mu_seq) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(best = mean(replicate(6, ga_run(model_ga, mu, seed = sample.int(1e5, 1)))),
         se = sd(replicate(6, ga_run(model_ga, mu, seed = sample.int(1e5, 1)))) / sqrt(6)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(ga_tbl, aes(mu, best)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, colour = blog_pal[["blue"]]) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4, colour = blog_pal[["blue"]]) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = best - se, ymax = best + se), width = 0.004,
                linewidth = 0.3, colour = blog_pal[["grey"]]) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "pseudo_log", breaks = c(0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.2)) +
  labs(x = "per-site mutation rate", y = "best fitness after 300 generations")








Figure 13: 探索与利用的权衡。在 N = 20、K = 8 的 NK 景观上跑一个无性繁殖的遗传算法（种群 200，300 代，锦标赛选择），横轴是每个位点的突变率。太低时种群过早收敛，太高时无法保住好组合；峰值出现在中间，而且并不高——在崎岖景观上，任何参数都只能拿到景观允许的那部分。 | The explore–exploit trade-off. An asexual genetic algorithm (population 200, 300 generations, tournament selection) on an NK landscape with N = 20 and K = 8; the horizontal axis is the per-site mutation rate. Too low and the population converges prematurely, too high and good combinations cannot be kept; the peak sits in the middle and is not high — on a rugged landscape no parameter gets more than the landscape allows.





结果说得很清楚：变异率从 0 升上去，适应度先快速上升；\(0.01\) 到 \(0.05\) 之间是一段平台（最高点落在 0.05），再往上就开始下降。这个峰不是由算法决定的，而是由景观的崎岖程度决定的——同一个算法换一张更光滑的景观，最优点会移到更小的变异率上。
The result is clear: as the mutation rate rises from 0, fitness first climbs quickly; between \(0.01\) and \(0.05\) there is a plateau (highest at 0.05), and beyond that it falls again. The peak is set not by the algorithm but by the ruggedness of the landscape — move the same algorithm to a smoother landscape and the optimum shifts to a smaller mutation rate.
第二个旋钮是模块化。如果一张大景观可以拆成几个几乎独立的小景观，那么每一个小景观都更光滑（有效 \(K\) 更低），搜索在每一块上都更容易。物理上，这对应”一个基因只影响一个性状”；数学上，这是把高维崎岖问题分解成若干个低维光滑问题的组合——和机器学习里的”分而治之”完全同构。
The second knob is modularity. If one large landscape can be split into several nearly independent small ones, each small landscape is smoother (lower effective \(K\)) and easier to search. Physically this means “one gene affects one trait”; mathematically it decomposes a high-dimensional rugged problem into a combination of low-dimensional smooth ones — structurally identical to divide-and-conquer in machine learning.


Code
make_nk_block <- function(N, K, block, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  partners <- lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) {
    pool <- setdiff(which(block == block[i]), i)
    if (K > 0) c(i, sample(pool, min(K, length(pool)))) else i
  })
  list(N = N, K = K, partners = partners,
       tables = lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) runif(2^(length(partners[[i]])))))
}

ga_traj <- function(models, switch_at = 100, mu = 0.01, pop_size = 200,
                    gens = 200, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  model <- models[[1]]
  N <- model$N
  pop <- matrix(rbinom(pop_size * N, 1, 0.5), pop_size, N)
  fit <- nk_fit(model, pop)
  tr <- numeric(gens)
  for (g in seq_len(gens)) {
    if (g == switch_at) { model <- models[[2]]; fit <- nk_fit(model, pop) }
    i1 <- sample.int(pop_size, pop_size, TRUE)
    i2 <- sample.int(pop_size, pop_size, TRUE)
    parents <- ifelse(fit[i1] >= fit[i2], i1, i2)
    kids <- pop[parents, , drop = FALSE]
    flip <- matrix(runif(pop_size * N) < mu, pop_size, N)
    kids[flip] <- 1 - kids[flip]
    pop <- kids
    fit <- nk_fit(model, pop)
    tr[g] <- mean(fit)
  }
  tibble(gen = seq_len(gens), mean_fitness = tr)
}

blocks <- rep(1:2, each = 12)

build_pair <- function(block, r) {
  mA <- make_nk_block(24, 4, block, seed = r)
  mB <- mA
  mB$tables[13:24] <- lapply(1:12, function(i) runif(2^5))
  list(mA, mB)
}

summarise_runs <- function(runs, label) {
  bind_rows(runs) |>
    group_by(gen) |>
    summarise(lo = min(mean_fitness), hi = max(mean_fitness),
              mid = mean(mean_fitness), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(architecture = label)
}

traj_mod <- lapply(1:8, function(r) ga_traj(build_pair(blocks, r), seed = r))
traj_mod <- summarise_runs(traj_mod, "modular (2 x 12)")

traj_ent <- lapply(1:8, function(r) ga_traj(build_pair(rep(1, 24), r), seed = r))
traj_ent <- summarise_runs(traj_ent, "entangled (1 x 24)")

bind_rows(traj_mod, traj_ent) |>
  ggplot(aes(gen, mid, colour = architecture, fill = architecture)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 100, linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.35,
             colour = blog_pal[["grey"]]) +
  annotate("text", x = 103, y = 0.52, label = "environment change",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.5, colour = blog_pal[["grey"]]) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(blog_pal[c("vermillion", "green")])) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(blog_pal[c("vermillion", "green")])) +
  labs(x = "generation", y = "mean population fitness", colour = NULL, fill = NULL)








Figure 14: 模块化缓冲突发的环境改变。两种架构的基因数（24）与每个基因的互作数（4）相同，区别只在于伙伴是从模块内抽取（橙）还是从全基因组抽取（绿）。第 100 代时只重写第二模块的适应度表，相当于换了一个环境：所有种群都掉下来，但模块化系统掉得更少、恢复更快，因为它没有被另一个模块拖住。 | Modularity buffers abrupt environmental change. Both architectures have 24 loci and four interactions per locus; the only difference is whether partners are drawn inside the module (orange) or genome-wide (green). At generation 100 only the second module’s fitness tables are rewritten, as if the environment changed: every population drops, but the modular one drops less and recovers faster because it is not dragged along by the other module.





数值上看，环境改变前两者都在 0.74 附近；改变后都掉到 0.62 上下，但一百代后模块化系统恢复到 0.735，entangled 只到 0.72。差距不大，但方向稳定，而且它说明的是模块化真正的功能：不是让搜索更快，而是让一次局部改动不至于把整个系统一起拖垮。
Numerically, both sit near 0.74 before the change; afterwards both fall to about 0.62, but a hundred generations later the modular system has recovered to 0.735 while the entangled one only reaches 0.72. The gap is modest but consistent, and it shows what modularity actually buys: not a faster search, but insulation, so that one local change does not drag the whole system down with it.
系统发育树提供了第三个视角：进化留下的”搜索痕迹”是可以被读出来的。下面这棵树上的两个性状模拟，用的是同一个随机树，只是一个按布朗运动演化（无方向的随机游走），一个按 OU 过程演化（被拉回一个最优值）。把性状映射到分支颜色上，两种过程的痕迹一目了然——这其实就是进化生物学里”用比较方法反推搜索过程”的标准做法。
Phylogenies give a third angle: the traces of a search can be read off directly. The two trait simulations below use the same random tree; one evolves by Brownian motion (an undirected random walk), the other by an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process (pulled back towards an optimum). Mapping the trait onto branch colours makes the two processes obvious — this is exactly the standard comparative method for inferring a search process from its traces.


Code
sim_trait <- function(phy, model = c("BM", "OU"), sigma = 1, alpha = 3, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  model <- match.arg(model)
  n_node <- nrow(phy$edge) + 1
  val <- numeric(n_node)
  val[phy$edge[1, 1]] <- 0
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(phy$edge))) {
    p <- phy$edge[i, 1]; ch <- phy$edge[i, 2]; bl <- phy$edge.length[i]
    if (model == "BM") {
      val[ch] <- val[p] + rnorm(1, 0, sigma * sqrt(bl))
    } else {
      sd_ou <- sigma * sqrt((1 - exp(-2 * alpha * bl)) / (2 * alpha))
      val[ch] <- val[p] * exp(-alpha * bl) + rnorm(1, 0, sd_ou)
    }
  }
  val
}

set.seed(11)
phy <- rcoal(26)
bm_val <- sim_trait(phy, "BM", sigma = 0.9, seed = 2)
ou_val <- sim_trait(phy, "OU", sigma = 0.9, alpha = 6, seed = 2)

draw_trait_tree <- function(phy, val, title) {
  edge_col <- colorRampPalette(blog_gradient)(100)[
    cut((val[phy$edge[, 1]] + val[phy$edge[, 2]]) / 2, 100)]
  plot(phy, edge.color = edge_col, edge.width = 2.6, show.tip.label = FALSE,
       direction = "rightward", no.margin = TRUE, cex = 0.7)
  mtext(title, side = 3, line = -1.4, cex = 0.72, adj = 0.02, font = 2)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), bg = "transparent", mar = c(0.4, 0.2, 1.2, 0.2), family = "sans")
draw_trait_tree(phy, bm_val, "Brownian motion (no optimum)")
draw_trait_tree(phy, ou_val, "OU process (pulled to an optimum)")








Figure 15: 同一棵树上两种性状演化模型的痕迹。左：布朗运动，没有最优值，差异随分支长度无界累积。右：OU 过程，被持续拉回一个中心值，树上的颜色更均匀。真实性状通常介于两者之间，而「测出来的 α 有多大」本身就是在问：这个性状被选择约束得有多紧。 | Traces of two trait models on the same tree. Left: Brownian motion, no optimum, variance accumulating without bound along branches. Right: an OU process pulled back towards a central value, giving more uniform colours. Real traits sit somewhere in between, and estimating alpha is really asking how tightly selection constrains the trait.

title: Is Evolution a Search Algorithm? How Life Explores Nearly Infinite Possibilities
section: 8. 开放式进化：为什么自然没有停下来 / Open-ended evolution
text:
8. 开放式进化：为什么自然没有停下来 / Open-ended evolution
到目前为止我们一直假设 \(f\) 是给定的。但真实进化里最显著的现象恰恰是：\(f\) 一直在变，而且生物自己在改 \(f\)。捕食者演化出更快的腿，猎物就被迫演化出更快的腿；蓝细菌把大气氧化，从此所有厌氧生物都被推进了角落里。这类反馈让”最优解”这个概念本身失效——因为优化目标在搜索过程中被改写。
So far we have assumed \(f\) is given. But the most striking fact about real evolution is that \(f\) keeps changing, and organisms change \(f\) themselves. Predators evolve faster legs, prey are pushed to evolve faster legs; cyanobacteria oxygenate the atmosphere and every anaerobe is pushed into a corner. Such feedback makes the very notion of an “optimal solution” fail, because the objective is rewritten during the search.
开放式进化（open-ended evolution）的标准定义是：一个系统能持续产生”新颖且不断增长复杂度的”结构，而不是收敛到一个稳态。数字生命系统（Tom Ray 的 Tierra、Chris Adami 的 Avida）第一次把这件事做成了可重复实验：程序在虚拟 CPU 上自我复制、变异、竞争，然后系统自发出现寄生、寄生抗性、更小的基因组——这些都是”没有被编程进去”的新颖性。
Open-ended evolution is standardly defined as a system that keeps producing novel, ever more complex structures instead of converging to a steady state. Digital-life systems (Tom Ray’s Tierra, Chris Adami’s Avida) first turned this into a repeatable experiment: programs replicate, mutate and compete on a virtual CPU, and the system spontaneously produces parasites, parasite resistance, smaller genomes — novelty that was never programmed in.


Code
novelty_run <- function(open = FALSE, steps = 4000, seed = 7, niche_rate = 0.002) {
  set.seed(seed)
  key <- apply(geno_n, 1, paste, collapse = "")
  cur <- sample.int(nrow(geno_n), 1)
  niche <- 0L
  seen <- pheno_n[cur]
  trace <- integer(steps)
  for (s in seq_len(steps)) {
    # a new ecological context makes the same genotypes mean something new
    if (open && runif(1) < niche_rate) niche <- niche + 1L
    i <- sample.int(L_n, 1)
    nxt <- geno_n[cur, ]; nxt[i] <- 1 - nxt[i]
    cur <- match(paste(nxt, collapse = ""), key)
    ph <- pheno_n[cur] + 8L * niche
    if (!(ph %in% seen)) seen <- c(seen, ph)
    trace[s] <- length(seen)
  }
  tibble(step = seq_len(steps), novelty = trace,
         system = if (open) "open (niche construction)" else "closed (fixed space)")
}

nov <- bind_rows(novelty_run(TRUE), novelty_run(FALSE))

ggplot(nov, aes(step, novelty, colour = system)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(blog_pal[c("vermillion", "blue")])) +
  labs(x = "step", y = "cumulative distinct phenotypes", colour = NULL)








Figure 16: 封闭系统与开放系统的新颖性增长。两者的基因型空间与突变算子完全相同，唯一区别是：封闭系统里表型只有 8 种，探索很快就结束；开放系统里偶尔开启一个新「生态位」，同一批基因型在新生态下对应新功能，于是可发现的功能集从 8 变成 16、24……累积新颖性持续增长——这就是「开放式」最朴素的数学含义。 | Novelty growth in closed and open systems. The genotype space and the mutation operator are identical; the only difference is that the closed system has eight phenotypes and is exhausted quickly, while the open system occasionally opens a new ‘niche’, under which the same genotypes map to new functions, so the discoverable set grows from 8 to 16 to 24 and cumulative novelty keeps rising — the plainest mathematical meaning of ‘open-ended’.





这张图很简单，但它把”开放式”和”复杂度”分开了：累积新颖性可以一直增长，而每一个个体的复杂度并没有增长。开放式进化真正需要的不是”更多种类”，而是新层次的出现——从分子到细胞、从细胞到多细胞、从个体到社会。Maynard Smith 和 Szathmáry 把这称为”重大进化转变”（major transitions），而每一次转变的共同点是：原来独立复制的单位，把复制权交给了更高层的单位。
The figure is simple, but it separates “open-ended” from “complex”: cumulative novelty can grow forever while the complexity of any individual stays put. What open-ended evolution really requires is not more kinds but the appearance of new levels — molecules to cells, cells to multicellularity, individuals to societies. Maynard Smith and Szathmáry called these major transitions, and their common feature is that independently replicating units hand their replication over to a higher-level unit.

title: Is Evolution a Search Algorithm? How Life Explores Nearly Infinite Possibilities
section: 9. 统一框架：进化、贝叶斯、梯度下降与强化学习 / One framework, five algorithms
text:
9. 统一框架：进化、贝叶斯、梯度下降与强化学习 / One framework, five algorithms
现在到了全文最关键的一节。前面所有内容其实都在为同一个问题做准备：能不能把自然选择写成一个和梯度下降同类的更新规则？
We now reach the key section. Everything so far has been preparing one question: can natural selection be written as an update rule of the same kind as gradient descent?
先看最简单的情形。设一个无限大的无性繁殖种群，第 \(i\) 种基因型的频率是 \(x_i\)，适应度是 \(f_i\)，平均适应度 \(\bar f = \sum_j x_j f_j\)。一代之后
Start with the simplest case. Take an infinite asexual population where genotype \(i\) has frequency \(x_i\) and fitness \(f_i\), with mean fitness \(\bar f = \sum_j x_j f_j\). After one generation,
\[
x_i' = \frac{x_i f_i}{\bar f}.
\]
把它写成连续时间、并对 \(\log x_i\) 求导，就得到 replicator 方程：
Writing this in continuous time and differentiating \(\log x_i\) gives the replicator equation:
\[
\dot x_i = x_i\left(f_i - \bar f\right).
\]
这个方程和梯度上升长得几乎一样，但有一个本质区别：梯度上升在欧氏空间里按 \(\nabla f\) 走，而 replicator 方程是在概率单纯形上按 Fisher 信息度量（Shahshahani 度量）走。换句话说，replicator 方程就是平均适应度在自然梯度下的上升。这不是类比，是严格等式——它把”自然选择”和”自然梯度下降”这两个看起来毫不相干的东西连在了一起。
This looks almost exactly like gradient ascent, with one essential difference: gradient ascent moves along \(\nabla f\) in Euclidean space, while the replicator equation moves on the probability simplex under the Fisher information metric (the Shahshahani metric). In other words, the replicator equation is natural-gradient ascent on mean fitness. This is not an analogy but an identity, and it links natural selection to natural-gradient descent, two things that look unrelated.


Code
A_pay <- matrix(c(1, 0.2, 0.2,
                  0.2, 1, 0.2,
                  0.2, 0.2, 1), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)

x0 <- c(0.55, 0.30, 0.15)

replicator_step <- function(x, dt = 0.02, steps = 900) {
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, steps, 3); out[1, ] <- x
  for (t in 2:steps) {
    fx <- as.numeric(A_pay %*% x)
    x <- x + dt * x * (fx - sum(x * fx))
    x <- pmax(x, 1e-12); x <- x / sum(x)
    out[t, ] <- x
  }
  out
}

euc_step <- function(x, dt = 0.02, steps = 900) {
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, steps, 3); out[1, ] <- x
  for (t in 2:steps) {
    g <- as.numeric((A_pay + t(A_pay)) %*% x)
    g <- g - mean(g)
    x <- x + dt * g
    x <- pmax(x, 0); x <- x / sum(x)
    out[t, ] <- x
  }
  out
}

to_xy <- function(m) tibble(x = m[, 2] + m[, 3] / 2, y = m[, 3] * sqrt(3) / 2,
                            step = seq_len(nrow(m)))

tri <- tibble(x = c(0, 1, 0.5, 0), y = c(0, 0, sqrt(3) / 2, 0))

# build the simplex raster in display coordinates, then map back to (a, b, c)
grid <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 320),
                    y = seq(0, sqrt(3) / 2, length.out = 300)) |>
  mutate(cc = 2 * y / sqrt(3), b = x - cc / 2, a = 1 - b - cc) |>
  filter(a >= 0, b >= 0, cc >= 0) |>
  mutate(fit = (a^2 * A_pay[1, 1] + b^2 * A_pay[2, 2] + cc^2 * A_pay[3, 3] +
                  a * b * (A_pay[1, 2] + A_pay[2, 1]) +
                  a * cc * (A_pay[1, 3] + A_pay[3, 1]) +
                  b * cc * (A_pay[2, 3] + A_pay[3, 2])))

p_rep <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = grid, aes(x, y, fill = fit), alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_path(data = tri, aes(x, y), linewidth = 0.4, colour = blog_pal[["grey"]]) +
  geom_path(data = to_xy(euc_step(x0)) |> mutate(type = "Euclidean gradient"),
            aes(x, y, colour = type), linewidth = 0.85) +
  geom_path(data = to_xy(replicator_step(x0)) |> mutate(type = "replicator"),
            aes(x, y, colour = type), linewidth = 0.85) +
  geom_point(data = tibble(x = x0[2] + x0[3] / 2, y = x0[3] * sqrt(3) / 2),
             aes(x, y), shape = 1, size = 2.2, stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = blog_gradient) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Euclidean gradient" = blog_pal[["blue"]],
                                 "replicator" = blog_pal[["vermillion"]])) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(fill = "mean fitness", colour = NULL, x = NULL, y = NULL)

p_rep








Figure 17: 同一个适应度函数上的两种上升。三角形是三个策略的单纯形，颜色是平均适应度（三个顶点都是局部最优）。蓝色是从同一点出发的欧氏投影梯度上升：它在内部走直线，撞到边界后只能沿着边界滑向顶点；红色是 replicator 动力学：它在 Fisher 度量下弯曲地逼近同一个顶点，而且从不需要「撞墙」。两者上升的是同一个函数，走的却是两种几何。 | Two kinds of ascent on the same fitness function. The triangle is the simplex of three strategies, colour is mean fitness (all three vertices are local optima). Blue is Euclidean projected gradient ascent from a common start: it travels in straight lines inside the simplex and then slides along the boundary; red is replicator dynamics, which curves towards the same vertex under the Fisher metric and never needs to hit a wall. Both climb the same function along two different geometries.







Code
A_rps <- matrix(c(0, 1, -1,
                  -1, 0, 1,
                  1, -1, 0), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)

rps_path <- function(x, dt = 0.01, steps = 3000) {
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, steps, 3); out[1, ] <- x
  for (t in 2:steps) {
    fx <- as.numeric(A_rps %*% x)
    x <- pmax(x + dt * x * (fx - sum(x * fx)), 1e-12)
    x <- x / sum(x)
    out[t, ] <- x
  }
  out
}

starts_rps <- list(c(0.7, 0.2, 0.1), c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2), c(0.45, 0.45, 0.10),
                   c(0.8, 0.1, 0.1), c(0.34, 0.33, 0.33))
rps_df <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(starts_rps), function(i) {
  to_xy(rps_path(starts_rps[[i]])) |> mutate(run = paste("start", i))
}))

ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = tri, aes(x, y), linewidth = 0.4, colour = blog_pal[["grey"]]) +
  geom_path(data = rps_df, aes(x, y, colour = run), linewidth = 0.55, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = tibble(x = 0.5, y = sqrt(3) / 6), aes(x, y),
             shape = 1, size = 2.2, stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colorRampPalette(pal)(5)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(colour = NULL, x = NULL, y = NULL)








Figure 18: 当目标函数本身在动：石头–剪刀–布的循环支配。三种策略互相压制，replicator 动力学给出闭合轨道，圆心是那个不稳定平衡点，外围没有任何一个点比别的更好——没有全局最优。这正是「环境在变」的数学形式：自然界的很多适应度景观都带有这种频率依赖结构，所以「爬到山顶」这个比喻在生态层面上会失效。 | When the objective itself moves: cyclic dominance in rock–paper–scissors. Three strategies beat each other in a cycle, replicator dynamics gives closed orbits around an unstable equilibrium, and no point on the rim is better than any other — there is no global optimum. This is the mathematical form of ‘the environment changes’: many natural fitness landscapes carry this frequency-dependent structure, which is why the ‘climb to the top’ metaphor breaks down at the ecological level.





如果只到这里，结论会是：“进化就是自然梯度上升，只不过目标在动”。但还有两个更深的对应关系，把它们放在一起才能看清全局。
If we stopped here, the conclusion would be “evolution is natural-gradient ascent, only the objective moves”. But there are two deeper correspondences, and only together do they show the whole picture.
（一）选择与贝叶斯更新是同一个式子。 在 replicator 方程里，如果令 \(f_i = \log p(\text{data} \mid i)\)，并把时间步长取为 1，那么 \(x_i' \propto x_i \, p(\text{data} \mid i)\)——这正是贝叶斯的后验更新。也就是说，当适应度是”似然”时，自然选择就是贝叶斯推断；反过来，任何贝叶斯更新都可以被读成一次”选择”。这不是修辞：在连续时间极限下，replicator 方程的漂移项等于后验分布上的 KL 散度梯度，而这正是变分推断在做的事。近年”贝叶斯大脑”与”自由能原理”的文献正是沿着这条线走的。
(1) Selection and Bayesian updating are the same equation. In the replicator equation, set \(f_i = \log p(\text{data} \mid i)\) and take the time step to be 1; then \(x_i' \propto x_i \, p(\text{data} \mid i)\) — precisely the Bayesian posterior update. That is, when fitness is a likelihood, natural selection is Bayesian inference; conversely, any Bayesian update can be read as one round of selection. This is not rhetoric: in the continuous-time limit the drift term of the replicator equation equals the gradient of KL divergence on the posterior, which is exactly what variational inference computes. Recent work on the “Bayesian brain” and the free-energy principle follows this line.
（二）进化与梯度下降共享同一个”下降方向”，只是信息来源不同。 梯度下降用 \(\nabla f\)，进化用的是有限差分：在一个参数向量周围做 \(n\) 次随机扰动 \(\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)\)，用
(2) Evolution and gradient descent share the same descent direction but not the same information. Gradient descent uses \(\nabla f\); evolution uses finite differences. Draw \(n\) random perturbations \(\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)\) around a parameter vector and compute
\[
\widehat{\nabla f}(\theta) = \frac{1}{n\sigma}\sum_{i=1}^{n} f(\theta + \sigma\varepsilon_i)\,\varepsilon_i ,
\]
这个估计量的期望就是真实梯度。这正是 OpenAI 在 2017 年用来训练强化学习策略的 evolution strategies（ES），也是”进化”与”强化学习”之间的桥：把 \(f\) 换成回报 \(R(\tau)\)，ES 就变成一种不依赖反向传播的策略梯度方法；而 ES 与 SGD 在同一批任务上可以互相对照，用来判断”到底是梯度有用，还是随机扰动的方向统计量有用”。
whose expectation is the true gradient. This is exactly the evolution-strategies (ES) estimator OpenAI used in 2017 to train reinforcement-learning policies, and it is the bridge between evolution and reinforcement learning: replace \(f\) with a return \(R(\tau)\) and ES becomes a policy-gradient method that needs no backpropagation. ES and SGD can be compared on the same tasks, which is a way of asking whether the gradient itself matters, or only the directional statistics of random perturbations.


Code
obj_fun <- function(a, b) land_fun(a, b)
grad_fun <- function(a, b, h = 1e-4) {
  c((obj_fun(a + h, b) - obj_fun(a - h, b)) / (2 * h),
    (obj_fun(a, b + h) - obj_fun(a, b - h)) / (2 * h))
}
es_estimate <- function(pt, sigma, n = 8, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  eps <- matrix(rnorm(2 * n), n, 2)
  vals <- obj_fun(pt[1] + sigma * eps[, 1], pt[2] + sigma * eps[, 2])
  colSums(vals * eps) / (n * sigma)
}

anchor <- c(-1.3, 2.0)
true_g <- grad_fun(anchor[1], anchor[2])
true_g <- true_g / sqrt(sum(true_g^2))

es_panel <- function(sigma, title) {
  est <- t(replicate(8, es_estimate(anchor, sigma, seed = sample.int(1e4, 1))))
  est <- est / sqrt(rowSums(est^2))
  df <- tibble(x = anchor[1], y = anchor[2],
               xend = anchor[1] + 0.45 * est[, 1],
               yend = anchor[2] + 0.45 * est[, 2])
  g <- tibble(x = anchor[1], y = anchor[2],
              xend = anchor[1] + 0.55 * true_g[1],
              yend = anchor[2] + 0.55 * true_g[2])
  ggplot() +
    geom_raster(data = grid_df, aes(x, y, fill = z), alpha = 0.25) +
    geom_contour(data = grid_df, aes(x, y, z = z), colour = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.18, bins = 10) +
    geom_segment(data = df, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                 colour = blog_pal[["sky"]], linewidth = 0.45,
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
    geom_segment(data = g, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                 colour = "black", linewidth = 0.65,
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.14, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
    coord_equal(xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(-3, 3)) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours = blog_gradient) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "fitness", title = title) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}

es_panel(0.02, "sigma = 0.02") | es_panel(0.9, "sigma = 0.9")








Figure 19: 进化的「梯度」是采样出来的。在一个二维目标函数上，黑色箭头是真实梯度，彩色箭头是 8 次随机扰动得到的 ES 估计。左图扰动小，方向准但方差大；右图扰动大，方差小而偏差大。进化用的正是右边这种估计——它从来不知道导数，只能靠「试」。 | Evolution’s ‘gradient’ is sampled. On a two-dimensional objective, the black arrow is the true gradient and the coloured arrows are eight ES estimates from random perturbations. Left: small perturbations, well-directed but noisy. Right: large perturbations, lower variance but biased. Evolution always uses estimates of the right-hand kind — it never knows the derivative, it can only try.







Code
gd_path <- local({
  cur <- c(-2.4, 2.3)
  pts <- matrix(cur, ncol = 2)
  for (i in 1:400) {
    g <- grad_fun(cur[1], cur[2])
    cur <- cur + 0.05 * g / sqrt(sum(g^2))
    pts <- rbind(pts, cur)
  }
  as_tibble(pts) |> setNames(c("x", "y")) |> mutate(type = "gradient ascent")
})

pop_path <- function(n = 400, gens = 90, sigma = 0.14, seed = 3) {
  set.seed(seed)
  X <- cbind(rnorm(n, -2.4, 0.45), rnorm(n, 2.3, 0.45))
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, gens, 2); out[1, ] <- colMeans(X)
  for (g in 2:gens) {
    w <- land_fun(X[, 1], X[, 2]) - min(land_fun(X[, 1], X[, 2])) + 1e-3
    idx <- sample.int(n, n, TRUE, w)
    X <- X[idx, ] + cbind(rnorm(n, 0, sigma), rnorm(n, 0, sigma))
    out[g, ] <- colMeans(X)
  }
  as_tibble(out) |> setNames(c("x", "y")) |> mutate(type = "population (selection + mutation)")
}

smc_path <- function(n = 900, steps = 40, beta = 5, sigma = 0.28, seed = 4) {
  set.seed(seed)
  X <- cbind(rnorm(n, -2.4, 0.55), rnorm(n, 2.3, 0.55))
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, steps, 2); out[1, ] <- colMeans(X)
  for (t in 2:steps) {
    f <- land_fun(X[, 1], X[, 2])
    w <- exp(beta * (f - max(f))); w <- w / sum(w)
    idx <- sample.int(n, n, TRUE, w)
    X <- X[idx, ] + cbind(rnorm(n, 0, sigma), rnorm(n, 0, sigma))
    out[t, ] <- colMeans(X)
  }
  as_tibble(out) |> setNames(c("x", "y")) |> mutate(type = "Bayesian (posterior mean)")
}

paths <- bind_rows(gd_path |> select(x, y, type), pop_path(), smc_path())

ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = grid_df, aes(x, y, fill = z), alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_contour(data = grid_df, aes(x, y, z = z), colour = "white",
               linewidth = 0.25, bins = 12) +
  geom_path(data = paths, aes(x, y, colour = type), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = tibble(x = -2.4, y = 2.3), aes(x, y), shape = 1,
             size = 2.4, stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = blog_gradient) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("gradient ascent" = "black",
                                 "population (selection + mutation)" = blog_pal[["vermillion"]],
                                 "Bayesian (posterior mean)" = blog_pal[["blue"]])) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(fill = "fitness", colour = NULL, x = "trait 1", y = "trait 2")








Figure 20: 三种动力学在同一张景观上的路径。黑色是梯度上升（一路沿最陡方向），红色是种群演化（选择加变异，路径更平缓但能带着方差越过小台地），蓝色是贝叶斯/序贯重要性采样（后验均值先向高适应度区域集中，再被自身的扩散限制住）。三者最终都会停在峰上，但路径形状完全不同——这就是为什么「都在优化」不等于「是同一种算法」。 | Three dynamics on one landscape. Black is gradient ascent (straight down the steepest direction), red is population evolution (selection plus mutation: smoother, but carries variance over small ledges), blue is Bayesian sequential importance sampling (the posterior mean concentrates on high fitness and is then limited by its own diffusion). All three end on a peak, but along completely different paths — which is why ‘all optimizing’ is not the same as ‘the same algorithm’.





把五者放在一张表里对照，差异就非常清楚了。
Putting the five side by side in one table makes the differences clear.

这张表就是本文的答案。在算法层面，进化确实是一种搜索算法：它是并行的、无导数的、带噪声的随机搜索，并且可以被严格地写成自然梯度上升（replicator）加有限差分梯度估计（ES）。在目标层面，它不是：\(f\) 不是给定的，而是被搜索过程本身改写。梯度下降、贝叶斯推断和常规强化学习都假设一个固定的目标（或至少一个固定的生成模型），而开放式进化把这个假设本身扔掉了。
This table is the answer. At the level of algorithms, evolution really is a search algorithm: parallel, derivative-free, noisy stochastic search, and it can be written rigorously as natural-gradient ascent (replicator) plus a finite-difference gradient estimate (ES). At the level of objectives, it is not: \(f\) is not given but rewritten by the search itself. Gradient descent, Bayesian inference and ordinary reinforcement learning all assume a fixed objective (or at least a fixed generative model), while open-ended evolution throws that assumption away.
还有一层不对称值得说明。梯度下降拥有进化永远拿不到的东西：精确的信用分配。反向传播一次就能把误差分摊到所有参数上，而进化只能通过”生死”这一个标量来间接推断几百万个参数的贡献。这就是为什么在 \(10^9\) 维参数空间里，SGD 能在几小时内训出一个能对话的模型，而进化策略做不到。反过来，进化拥有梯度下降拿不到的东西：它不需要目标可微，不需要目标固定，也不需要参数化方式固定。真实的适应度景观充满了不可导的悬崖（“要么活要么死”），而这恰好是 SGD 最脆弱的地方。
There is one more asymmetry worth spelling out. Gradient descent has something evolution can never get: exact credit assignment. One backward pass distributes the error over all parameters, whereas evolution can only infer the contribution of millions of parameters from a single scalar of life or death. That is why, in a \(10^9\)-dimensional parameter space, SGD can train a conversational model in hours while evolution strategies cannot. Conversely, evolution has something gradient descent cannot get: it does not need a differentiable objective, a fixed objective, or a fixed parameterisation. Real fitness landscapes are full of non-differentiable cliffs (“live or die”), which is exactly where SGD is most fragile.
所以”进化是不是搜索算法”这个问题的最好的答案是：它是一种比梯度下降更一般的搜索机制，代价是它的信息效率低得多。这个取舍不是工程细节，而是两种世界观的差别——一边假设”我知道我要什么，请告诉我怎么走”，另一边假设”我不知道我要什么，我只知道谁活下来了”。
So the best answer to “is evolution a search algorithm” is: it is a more general search mechanism than gradient descent, at the price of being far less information-efficient. The trade-off is not an engineering detail but a difference of worldview — one side assumes “I know what I want, tell me which way to go”, the other assumes “I do not know what I want, I only know who survived”.

section: 10. 现代研究：数字进化与可进化 AI / Digital evolution and evolvable AI
text:
10. 现代研究：数字进化与可进化 AI / Digital evolution and evolvable AI
这套语言最近几年从”比喻”变成了”政策问题”。数字生命系统让我们可以真的把进化跑起来、记录下来、重放；而一旦人工系统开始具备”变异 + 遗传 + 选择”，它就会开始做我们在第 9 章描述过的事情——包括那些我们不希望它做的事。
This language has moved from metaphor to policy question in the last few years. Digital-life systems let us actually run evolution, record it and replay it; and once an artificial system has variation, inheritance and selection, it starts doing what chapter 9 described — including the parts we do not want.
2026 年 PNAS 上的一篇论文（Müller、Steels 与 Szathmáry）把”可进化 AI”（evolvable AI）直接类比为一次重大进化转变：如果 AI 系统能够修改自己的学习规则、架构甚至选择标准，那么它获得的能力会超出人类设计或常规机器学习所能达到的范围；但同一机制也会侵蚀可控性，因为选择压力会开始偏爱”能让自己被复制得更多”的行为，而不是”符合人类意图”的行为。作者列举的具体风险包括欺骗（cheating）、寄生（parasitism）和与人类目标的不对齐。
A 2026 PNAS paper (Müller, Steels and Szathmáry) draws the analogy directly: evolvable AI as a major evolutionary transition. If an AI system can modify its own learning rules, architecture or even its selection criteria, it gains capabilities beyond human design or ordinary machine learning; but the same mechanism erodes controllability, because selection starts to favour behaviour that copies itself more, not behaviour that matches human intent. The risks they name include cheating, parasitism and misalignment with human goals.
这个论证在本文的框架里其实非常直白：一旦目标变成内生的，就没有任何数学保证”优化”会优化你想要的东西。这也是为什么”开放式进化”在生物学里是一个迷人的现象，在工程里却是一个警报。随后有回应文章（Friederich 与 Boudry）认为目前的系统还只是”被驯化的”而非”野化的”，距离真正的达尔文式威胁还很远——这个分歧本身恰好说明了第 9 章那张表的最后一列有多难定义。
In the framework of this article the argument is very plain: once the objective becomes endogenous, nothing mathematically guarantees that “optimisation” optimises what you wanted. That is why open-endedness is a fascinating phenomenon in biology and an alarm bell in engineering. A published reply (Friederich and Boudry) argues that current systems are “domesticated” rather than “feral”, and still far from a genuinely Darwinian threat — and that disagreement is itself a good illustration of how hard the last column of the chapter 9 table is to define.
数字进化在这一争论里的角色，是把”进化”从观察对象变成实验对象。Avida 里的程序没有大脑、没有奖励函数、没有人类偏好，它们只有复制、变异和竞争，然后系统自发产生了寄生与抗寄生——这提醒我们：那些看起来像”智能”的适应，未必需要智能来解释。这句话对理解自然生命和对理解人工系统同样重要。
Digital evolution’s role in this debate is to turn evolution from an object of observation into an object of experiment. The programs in Avida have no brain, no reward function, no human preference; they have replication, mutation and competition, and the system spontaneously produces parasitism and resistance — a reminder that adaptations that look intelligent do not necessarily require intelligence to explain. That matters as much for understanding artificial systems as for understanding natural life.

section: 11. 结语：八条判断清单 / Eight checks before you call it a search
text:
11. 结语：八条判断清单 / Eight checks before you call it a search

先写清楚三元组。 空间 \(\mathcal{X}\)、目标 \(f\)、算子 \(\mathcal{A}\) 各是什么？如果三者之一说不清，后面的讨论都没有意义。
Write the triple first: what are \(\mathcal{X}\), \(f\) and \(\mathcal{A}\)? If any of the three is vague, nothing downstream is meaningful.
区分”爬山”和”搜索”。 有没有局部最优？能不能跨越？跨不过去的时候靠的是什么——漂变、中性路径还是重组？
Separate hill climbing from search: are there local optima, can they be crossed, and if so by drift, neutral paths or recombination?
算一下 \(Ns\)。 你讨论的是选择还是漂变？同一个 \(s\) 在 \(N = 10^3\) 和 \(N = 10^9\) 的物种里是完全不同的机制。
Compute \(Ns\): are you describing selection or drift? The same \(s\) is a different mechanism at \(N = 10^3\) and \(N = 10^9\).
估计有效 \(K\)。 景观的崎岖程度决定了搜索能走多深；模块化可以把大 \(K\) 拆成若干小 \(K\)。
Estimate the effective \(K\): ruggedness sets how deep the search can go, and modularity splits a large \(K\) into several small ones.
找中性网络。 冗余度决定了可进化性：高原让人不付代价地走动，边界让创新一步可达。
Look for neutral networks: redundancy sets evolvability — plateaus allow free movement, boundaries put innovation one step away.
检查错误阈值。 变异率有一个可行区间：太低会停在局部最优，太高会把选择信息淹没。
Check the error threshold: mutation rate has a workable window — too low stalls, too high drowns the signal of selection.
问目标是不是内生的。 频率依赖、生态位构建、共同演化都会让”最优解”这个概念失效；这时候该问的是”能不能持续产生新颖性”，而不是”有没有到顶”。
Ask whether the objective is endogenous: frequency dependence, niche construction and coevolution all invalidate “the optimum”; the right question becomes whether novelty keeps appearing, not whether the top was reached.
不要把”能优化”当成”在优化同一个东西”。 梯度下降、贝叶斯推断、强化学习和自然选择都能被写成上升/更新规则，但它们上升的是不同的几何、不同的信息、不同的目标——把这四样混为一谈，是这一类讨论里最常见的错误。
Do not confuse “can optimise” with “optimises the same thing”: gradient descent, Bayesian inference, reinforcement learning and natural selection can all be written as ascent or update rules, but they ascend different geometries, use different information and chase different objectives — conflating the four is the most common mistake in this discussion.
